current_focus.domain: cms-sync-011: how seed/seed.json (copy, imagery slots, block types) and the EmDash CMS on repoglance.com stay equal so the live site never silently diverges from the locked content again; the sync model, its identity and trigger, and the live-equals-seed check
current_focus.summary: Maintainer 'go' on 2026-10-07 to: (1) emdash-upgrade-012: pin emdash and @emdash-cms/cloudflare to 1.2.0 exactly in package.json and scripts/audit-repo.mjs via npm, verify on it; (2) cms-sync-011 option D: scripts/cms-sync.mjs (--check default, read-only diff of block types and pages between seed/seed.json and the CMS, exit 1 on drift; --apply writes block types first, compatible in place and breaking as a new activated version, then pages as drafts with the revision token and block migration, then publish, then re-check; identity: cloudflared access token for the live site, EMDASH_TOKEN or EMDASH_HEADERS passthrough, dev bypass on localhost; never prints a header or token), scripts/live-check.mjs (npm run check:live: local workerd seed render of / and /testers compared with the live <main>, reports data-content-source, fails with a diff), a shared workerd helper for smoke and the live check, package scripts cms:check, cms:sync, check:live; docs: README status, docs/cms-access.md sync section plus the deploy runbook step (deploy, sync, live check) and the unattended service-token path as a documented unbuilt option, one AGENTS.md boundary line (the CMS is written only by the sync from the seed), docs/content.md pointer; proof under proof/cms-sync-20261007/PROOF.md and .grilltrack/proof/cms-sync-011-verify-20261007.md. Verification: unit checks of the diff logic; a dev-server round trip (CMS set up from the seed, driven to the 1 October state, synced back, check reports equal), the dev pages' data-content-source=cms render compared with the production build's seed render; npm run verify via mise; a read-only read of the live site. Then a separate read-only review on the exact commit, adjudication, ledger records, commit with the trailer, push, PR against main. The CMS/seed comparison is modulo block _version (seed stays at version 1; the CMS moves to version 2 because removing owner-filter is breaking). Maintainer gates after merge: deploy, cloudflared access login, npm run cms:sync, npm run check:live. No merge, deploy, Cloudflare, DNS, Access or secret action by the agent.

decisions.choice: D (maintainer, 2026-10-07): the seed stays the only source of truth; scripts/cms-sync.mjs upserts the seed's block types and pages into the CMS through EmDash's API and publishes them, so the CMS is the live source again and equal to the seed (fields and data equal; the CMS's block-type version numbers follow its own history, so the comparison is modulo _version); identity: the maintainer's own Cloudflare Access login cached by cloudflared (cf-access-token), no service token, no Access policy change, no API token, no guard change; trigger: a maintainer step right after every deploy (deploy, sync, live check), never on merge; scripts/live-check.mjs compares the live <main> of both pages with a seed render of the local build and reports data-content-source, failing on any difference.

decisions.question: How do seed/seed.json (copy, imagery slots, block types) and the EmDash CMS on repoglance.com stay equal, so the live site never silently diverges from the locked content again: which is the source, how does it reach the other, with which identity and trigger, and what proves the live site equals the seed?
decisions.rationale: Maintainer's answer 'D' to the four options presented with their gates and costs. Facts behind the shape: EmDash 1.0.1's client and CLI accept a cloudflared-cached Access JWT (cf-access-token), so the maintainer's own identity drives the API with no new Cloudflare resource; a service-token JWT carries no email and would need a Service Auth policy, a service token, an EmDash API token and a guard change (documented as the unattended option, not built); removing a select option is a breaking block-type change in EmDash 1.0.1, so the sync creates and activates a new version and migrates the blocks; the CMS must be written only after the Worker that renders the new seed is deployed, so the trigger is the deploy runbook, never the merge. Options A (seed only), B (sync without the live check) and C (CMS as source, seed exported) were not chosen. Builds on the closed track's site-copy-006, site-imagery-007 and cms-access-008 (.grilltrack/archive/gt-20261001102301-89ec89/).

decisions.choice: EmDash 1.2.0 with @emdash-cms/cloudflare 1.2.0 (published 2026-10-06 22:13 UTC), pinned exactly in package.json and in scripts/audit-repo.mjs, installed with npm (not the upgrade-emdash tool, which writes an ignored .emdash/UPGRADE.md and refreshes agent skills outside the repo's review path). Verified against the 1.0.1 baseline before the change: the block-type compatibility rules (a removed select option is breaking), the content update body (migrateBlocks, replaceBlocks, _rev), the Bearer-first auth middleware and the X-EmDash-Request rule, the emdash/client, emdash/client/cf-access and emdash/seed exports, the Blocks component, the middleware.outer option and the Cloudflare adapter's Access authenticate and worker entry are unchanged; 1.2.0 adds two core migrations (090_redirect_enable_loop_guard, 091_redirect_artifacts) that the default auto migration mode applies at runtime on the first request after the deploy; 1.2.0 adds syncName for Access (default true, unchanged behaviour), numbered pagination for content lists, the video block, admin.locales and the domain-change dialog, none of which this site uses.

decisions.question: Which EmDash release does repoglance.com run while the CMS sync is built?
decisions.rationale: Maintainer, 2026-10-07: 'actually, we need to be on emdash 1.2 that just released this morning'. Done inside cms-sync-011's cycle so the sync script is written and verified on the release the site will run.
decisions.verification_ref: run:npm run verify (audit 151 files, astro check 0/0, content 9/9, guard 11/11, edge 14/14, build, smoke 124/124)

pause.next_safe_action: After the maintainer's deploy, sync and live check: record the delivery and production results (the CMS equal to the seed, the live source cms, the live check equal) in proof/cms-sync-20261007/PROOF.md and the ledger, then open live-check-schedule-013 or the chosen alternative; if main moves before the merge, merge origin/main into claude/cms-sync with the ledger united and re-verify.
pause.reason: cms-sync-011 and emdash-upgrade-012 implemented, verified and reviewed clean (cms-sync-011 at git:54b213bef91986b09807aa177ea9f0da1c5a18ac after round 1 at git:0890336b5343f136019d9dd387934dc95497cc96; emdash-upgrade-012 at git:0890336b5343f136019d9dd387934dc95497cc96); delivered as PR saari-co/repoglance-site#10 on the maintainer's instruction. Waiting on the maintainer's gates: merge after CI is green and a review is clean on the exact head, deploy, cloudflared access login, npm run cms:sync, npm run check:live.

alternatives: screenshot-options-011: the hygiene round on the seed's screenshot options the first track deferred (retire or re-word the unused connect-or-explore-sample option, catch orphan WebPs under public/screenshots/), which now also decides whether the sync should prune inactive block-type versions (review round 1, finding 3).

site-links-010 and the Play opt-in link: maintainer actions outside the repo (the Play listing's website field, the RepoGlance README pointing at repoglance.com, the opt-in link when Play Console shows it), each a seed change that reaches the live site through cms:sync and check:live.
recommendation.reason: The sync and the live check exist and are proven locally, but both run only when the maintainer runs them; the invariant the maintainer asked for ('never silently diverges') is strongest when the live check also runs on a schedule. The other candidates are hygiene or outside actions, not product decisions.
recommendation.recommended: live-check-schedule-013: run scripts/live-check.mjs unattended as a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow against https://repoglance.com (daily, plus workflow_dispatch), building main and failing loudly on any <main> difference or a non-seed, non-synced source; no secrets, no Cloudflare change, the pages are public. It closes the gap this cycle leaves between maintainer runs: drift is caught within a day instead of at the next deploy.
